activity.notes: After the death of his father Gaia during the succession crisis around 206 BCE, Masinissa returned to Africa and recovered the Massylian throne from the rival succession centered on Lacumazes. Syphax soon defeated him and drove him from his kingdom. ATLAS therefore records this short first Massylian reign separately and preserves the real interruption rather than extending his later Numidian kingship backward.

sources.title: Masinissa — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: Oxford states that after his father's death Masinissa returned to Africa, recovered control of his kingdom from his nephew, and was then driven out again by Syphax.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Book 29, chapter 30 — Perseus
sources.citation_text: Livy's narrative records Masinissa's return after the deaths in the Massylian succession and his campaign to recover his father's kingdom.
